extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, and general internet news consumers interested in media literacy and assessing news sources
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating news and information websites using NewsGuard's nine journalistic criteria and its Nutrition Label/rating system to determine credibility and transparency. Includes interpreting shield icons and Green/Yellow/Red/Satire/Platform category meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not repeatedly publish false content
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not repeatedly publish false content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under NewsGuard's 'Credibility' criteria. Analysts check whether a site repeatedly publishes verifiably false information; points are assigned toward the site's overall credibility score based on this assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathers and presents information responsibly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Credibility' criteria. Evaluators consider sourcing practices, fact-gathering methods, balance, and whether reporting reflects responsible journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly corrects or clarifies errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'Credibility.' Sites are assessed for having a corrections policy/practice and whether they timely acknowledge and fix mistakes; this affects their Credibility points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Credibility dimension: sites are evaluated on whether opinion and analysis are clearly labeled and separated from factual news reporting to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility check for whether headlines accurately reflect article content (not sensational, misleading, or clickbait); deceptive headlines reduce the site's credibility score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website discloses ownership and financing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Transparency.' Evaluators look for clear disclosure of who owns and funds the site as part of assessing potential biases or agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly labels advertising
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency criterion: advertising and sponsored content should be clearly labeled so readers can distinguish it from editorial content; failures reduce transparency points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals who’s in charge, including possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveals who’s in charge, including possible conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency dimension: sites should identify editors/managers and disclose any conflicts of interest that could affect coverage; absence of such disclosures lowers transparency scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides names of content creators and contact/biographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides the names of content creators, along with either contact or biographical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency criterion: by naming authors and providing contact or biography information, sites increase accountability and transparency; anonymous or unsigned content scores lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating categories (Green / Yellow / Red / Satire / Platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard analysts assign each site one of five rating categories: 'Green' (overall approval/reliable), 'Yellow' (sufficient but use with caution), 'Red' (overall disapproval/warning), 'Satire', or 'Platform'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: AP News shown as Green with credibility score 95.0/100; The Onion shown Yellow (satirical/not serious news); Drudge Report shown Red (does not run corrections or acknowledge its agenda). Note: a Green rating does not guarantee a score of 100. NewsGuard posts full reports explaining the reasoning behind each category assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition Label system and shield icon presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard uses a 'Nutrition Label' system and shield icon to present ratings for news sources; labels appear in searches and on social media links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After installing NewsGuard, sites and social media posts show a shield icon representing reliability. Nutrition Labels summarize the site's performance on the nine criteria and link to full reports with detailed explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring approach: points assigned per criterion / full report transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the nine journalistic criteria can earn a certain number of points; cumulative points determine a site's score and category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts assign points for each criterion and publish full reports explaining the reasoning behind scores. The page notes that sites rated cover over 4,500 websites accounting for 95% of news engagement in several countries. The scoring system means that meeting some criteria may compensate partially for failures in others and that a 'Green' rating is not necessarily a perfect numerical score.
